solution.justification: Joint torque is the signed moment component along the permitted rotation axis, not a generic moment magnitude.

optionExplanations.o1: The scalar effort is n_i dot z_i.
optionExplanations.o2: Norm discards sign and is not generally the joint-axis projection.
optionExplanations.o3: The revolute axes are z, not the link directions.
optionExplanations.o4: A one-DOF revolute actuator supplies one scalar generalized effort.

formulas.expression: f_i=R_i,i+1 f_(i+1)+F_i; n_i=N_i+R_i,i+1 n_(i+1)+rCi×F_i+p_i,i+1×(R_i,i+1 f_(i+1)); tau_i=n_i·z_i

variables.f_i,f_(i+1): transmitted forces expressed in their own link frames
variables.F_i: own mass force in frame i
variables.n_i,n_(i+1): transmitted moments about respective frame origins
variables.N_i: own COM spin moment in frame i
variables.R_i,i+1: rotation from downstream frame to frame i
variables.rCi: origin i to COM i, in frame i
variables.p_i,i+1: origin i to next origin, in frame i
variables.z_i: positive unit joint axis in frame i

assumptions: Use the lecture’s vertical-plane two-revolute model: massless links of positive lengths l1,l2, endpoint point masses m1,m2, theta1 measured counterclockwise from +X0, theta2 relative to link1, +Y0 upward, physical gravity −g Y0 with g≥0. Positive joint torques increase their joint angles. No terminal wrench, friction or motor inertia unless explicitly changed.

stem: Which sequence respects the dependencies of the recursive inverse-dynamics algorithm?

options.text: Inward actuator torques first, then compute the COM accelerations needed to obtain those torques
Outward force recursion from the base load, then inward joint velocities from the terminal load
Perform only the outward pass because the local COM moment already equals joint torque
Outward kinematics and link inertia forces/moments, then inward transmitted loads and actuator efforts

citations.locator: Lecture13, physical PDF page 425, printed slide 22: Outward then inward Newton–Euler passes
citations.evidenceText:
Summary

•  The complete algorithm for computing joint
   torques from the motion of the joints is
  composed of two parts.
•  First, link velocities and accelerations are
   iteratively computed from link 1 out to link 𝑛
  and the Newton—Euler equations are applied
   to each link.
•  Second, for given forces and torques of
   interaction at EE, joint actuator torques are
  computed recursively from link 𝑛 back to link 1.

solution.justification: Motion propagates outward from the base; required loads propagate inward from the prescribed terminal boundary.

optionExplanations.o3: The inward pass uses quantities computed in the outward pass.
optionExplanations.o1: This swaps the data and propagation directions.
optionExplanations.o2: The inward lever-arm and downstream-load accumulation is still required.

steps: Initialize the fixed-base/gravity data and prescribed joint motion.
Compute link velocities, accelerations, F_i and N_i outward.
Initialize the terminal wrench and propagate f_i,n_i inward.
Project each joint moment onto its positive joint axis.
